mechanism_narrative: The federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) being at its current level (3.0%) is always associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as low interest rates reduce the cost of capital and increase the present value of future cash flows.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS is reported (over a 10-year rolling window), or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) rises above 195.0 (May 2005 baseline), it signals accelerating inflation that leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, as higher inflation erodes real returns and prompts monetary tightening.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 195.0 (over a 10-year rolling window), or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When both GDP growth (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) are above their 12-month moving averages, it signals a robust demand environment that leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, as strong consumer and business activity supports corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when both GDPC1 and HOUST are above their 12-month moving averages (over a 10-year rolling window), or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In regimes where the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 5.0%, it signals a weak labor market that leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, as high unemployment reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE > 5.0 (over a 10-year rolling window), or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 115.0 (May 2005 baseline), it signals a contraction in the industrial sector that leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, as supply chain disruptions and reduced manufacturing output dampen economic growth and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO < 115.0 (over a 10-year rolling window), or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is rising and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is above 195.0, it signals a monetary tightening cycle that leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, as rising rates and persistent inflation pressure reduce equity valuations.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS is rising and CPIAUCSL > 195.0 (over a 10-year rolling window), or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In regimes where industrial production (INDPRO) is below 115.0, it signals a supply contraction that leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, as reduced manufacturing output and supply chain bottlenecks suppress economic growth and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO < 115.0 (over a 10-year rolling window), or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the number of employees (PAYEMS) falls below 133000.0 (May 2005 baseline), it signals a weakening labor market that leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days, as declining employment reduces consumer spending and corporate revenue growth.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when PAYEMS < 133000.0 (over a 10-year rolling window), or the Rank IC is below 0.03.
